January 30, 19.

Sir Everard D. H. Fraser, K.C.M.G.,
H. B. M. Consul-General,
Shanghai.

My dear Sir Everard, Confidential.
In regard to your letter of January
18, addressed to Captain Barrett, various enquiries
were requested and amongst them a report on the Chinese
Red Cross Society was asked for. I now have to
convey to you the following information, but may
state that there is no record here of the Police
having been asked in October 1917 to report on this
same subject.-
The Russo-Japanese war having brought home to Chinese
the importance of the medical branch of armies in the
field, Messrs. Li Hai Hsuan (吕海寰), a former Taotai
of Shanghai, and Shen Tun Ho (沈敦和), who came into
prominence as a result of his humane treatment of foreign-
ers during the Boxer Rebellion, decided to start a branch
of the Red Cross Society in China. They enlisted the
services of Dr. J. C. Ferguson, an ex American missionary,
who is now adviser to the Central Government, and estab-
lished an office in Peking with a branch in Shanghai.
The society was a very humble institution at first but
its influence soon spread, and branches were established
in various parts of the country. Probably for the first
time in the history of China, the Red Cross made an
organized attempt to relieve distress caused by famine, etc.

1919年1月30日。

致 艾弗拉德·D·H·弗雷泽爵士，K.C.M.G.，
英国驻上海总领事。

亲爱的弗雷泽爵士，机密。
关于你1月18日致巴雷特上尉的信件，
其中要求进行了多项调查，其中包括要求提供
一份关于中国红十字会的报告。现将以下信息
转达给你，但需说明的是，此处并无记录显示
警方曾在1917年10月被要求就同一主题提交
报告。——
日俄战争使中国人认识到军队中医务部门在
战场上的重要性，前上海道台吕海寰先生和在
义和团运动期间因对外国人的人道待遇而崭露头角的
沈敦和先生，决定在中国创办红十字会分会。他们
聘请了前美国传教士、现任中央政府顾问的J. C. 弗格森
博士的服务，并在北京设立办事处，在上海设立分部。
该会起初规模很小，但其影响力迅速扩大，并在全国
各地建立了分会。这或许是中国历史上第一次，红十字
会有组织地尝试缓解由饥荒等引起的苦难。

The reputation of the Red Cross has suffered considerably
in late years. Chinese, who previously had great faith in
the probity of its officials, now doubt their honesty.
There seems to be some ground for these suspicions, and it
is known that Shen Tun Ho some months ago paid $5,000.00
to an ex employee, who is said to have threatened to expose
irregularities in the administration.

Yours sincerely,

Captain-Superintendent of Police.

近年来，红十字会的声誉遭受了严重损害。
此前对其官员廉洁性深信不疑的中国人，现在怀疑
他们的诚实。这些怀疑似乎有一定依据，据悉，沈敦和
在几个月前向一名前雇员支付了5,000.00美元，据称
该雇员曾威胁要揭露管理中的违规行为。

此致
敬礼，

警务处处长。

29th January, 1919.

REPORT ON The Chinese Red Cross Society, at Request of British
Consulate.

Made by D.S.I. Givens. Forwarded by Chief Detective Officer.

Sir,

The Russo-Japanese war having brought home to Chinese
the importance of the medical branch of armies in the field,
Messrs. Li Hai Hsuan (吕海寰), a former Taotai of Shanghai,
and Shen Tun Ho (沈敦和), who came into prominence as a
result of his humane treatment of foreigners during the Boxer
Rebellion, decided to start a branch of the Red Cross Society
in China. They enlisted the services of Dr. J. C. Ferguson,
an ex American missionary, who is now Adviser to the Central
Government, and established an office in Peking with a branch
in Shanghai. The society was a very humble institution at
first but its influence soon spread, and branches were
established in various parts of the country. Probably for
the first time in the history of China, the Red Cross made an
organized attempt to relieve distress caused by famine, etc.
The beneficial work of which it was capable soon became
apparent to the personnel of the Government, officials and
wealthy merchants who generously supported it.

The Red Cross Society continued to prosper and gained in
public esteem to such an extent that for several years some of
the most highly placed natives and foreigners in this country
associated themselves with it as members of its various
committees, and as a result of their exertions it was
recognized by the Geneva Convention in 1906.

The British and American residents have from the

先生，

日俄战争使中国人认识到军队中医务部门在
战场上的重要性，前上海道台吕海寰先生和在
义和团运动期间因对外国人的人道待遇而崭露头角的
沈敦和先生，决定在中国创办红十字会分会。他们
聘请了前美国传教士、现任中央政府顾问的J. C. 弗格森
博士的服务，并在北京设立办事处，在上海设立分部。
该会起初规模很小，但其影响力迅速扩大，并在全国
各地建立了分会。这或许是中国历史上第一次，红十字
会有组织地尝试缓解由饥荒等引起的苦难。其所能从事
的有益工作很快引起了政府人员、官员和富商的注意，
并得到了他们的慷慨支持。

红十字会继续蓬勃发展，公众声望大增，以至于
几年来，一些在华地位最高的华人和外国人都以各
委员会成员的身份参与其中，由于他们的努力，该会
于1906年获得《日内瓦公约》的认可。

英美居民从一开始就在协助中国红十字会工作的
外国人中处于领先地位。德国人似乎从未显著参与其
活动，但一位

B.M.Consulate General,
Shanghai.
January 11th., 1919.

Dear Captain Farrett,

The Consul General would like the
offices of L.Everett, 1A Jinkee Road, to be watched
for a week. He used, as you know, to aid the enemy
actively, and a reference to visits to him in your
report about C.H.S.Bryant makes it look as if he may
still be playing tricks.

The following is from a despatch from
Hankow:- "A mysterious individual calling himself
a mining prospector, and purporting to have Dutch
papers, arrived at the Settlement on the 7th instant
and thrust himself upon the hospitality of several
British subjects, who declined to have anything
to do with him.....I have been unable to learn his
name but strongly suspect that he is a 'stitute
German." Is anyone known to you and answering to
this description missing from here?

Yours,

（批：Dealt with J.O.2487）
（批：Dealt with J.O.2477）

英国驻上海总领事馆，
上海。
1919年1月11日。

亲爱的法雷特上尉：

总领事希望派人监视金基路1A号
L. Everett 的住所一周。如您所知，他过去曾
积极援助敌人，而在您关于C.H.S. Bryant的报告中
提到有人拜访他，这看起来好像他可能仍在搞鬼。

以下是来自汉口的一份急件：“一个自称是
矿产勘探者、声称持有荷兰证件的神秘人物，于
本月7日抵达租界，强行要求几位英国侨民提供
款待，但这些侨民拒绝与他有任何瓜葛……我未能
查明他的姓名，但强烈怀疑他是一个‘冒牌’
德国人。”这里是否有符合此描述且为您所知的
失踪人员？

此致，
